page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-48 is a general-purpose server powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. It features 48 virtual CPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing two threads per core. The system is configured with 192.0 GB of dedicated system memory, maintaining a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPU accelerators.

In benchmark testing, the n2d-standard-48 demonstrates strong CPU performance, scoring in the top 25% for both single-core and multi-core stress-ng evaluations, as well as the PassMark CPU suite. Cryptographic capabilities are also strong, supported by hardware-accelerated AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instruction sets, which is reflected in its high PassMark CPU encryption score. Memory performance is robust, with a PassMark memory score in the top 25% and uncached read bandwidth reaching 109.91 GB/sec.

Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated CPU allocation, this server is designed for general-purpose enterprise workloads, multi-threaded software compilation, and medium-scale database operations. While it lacks local NVMe SSDs and GPU accelerators, its strong multi-core processing and memory bandwidth make it highly capable for web serving, text processing, and small-to-medium language model inference tasks.
